This study offers a meta-analysis of 12 anomaly detectors evaluated in a prior study, examining their performance across 11 datasets. We investigate the influence of various hyperparameters and assess how the results of the earlier experiment were affected by specific methodological choices. Additionally, we explore the potential for enhancing those outcomes.

Gliomas are the most prevalent type of brain tumor, accounting for approximately 85% of all cases. While the standard of care for gliomas involves surgical resection, the procedure is highly complex and demands significant expertise. Consequently, there is a critical need for automated tools to assist in surgical planning and intraoperative decision-making. This study introduces a deep learning-based approach for segmenting gliomas in MRI scans, utilizing a U-Net architecture enhanced with skip connections. The model was trained on 100 manually annotated MRI images from the BraTS 2019 dataset, which includes labels for the tumor core, enhancing tumor, and edema. To address the class imbalance inherent in the data, we applied the focal loss function. Furthermore, we implemented a post-processing technique based on the watershed algorithm to refine the model's output. The results demonstrate that this proposed method achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We introduce a new approach to generate a triplon current in solids, which involves applying a magnetic field gradient across a ferromagnet-antiferromagnet heterostructure. This method is applicable to any solid exhibiting an antiferromagnetic phase.

This study introduces a new form of net convergence, termed statistical convergence, which extends the concept of statistically convergent sequences. We demonstrate that this convergence satisfies specific fundamental properties and establish its relationship with classical convergence. Furthermore, we prove that the limit operation for statistical convergence of nets is unique. The work concludes by examining the relationship between the statistical density of subsets within a directed set and the statistical convergence of nets defined over those sets.

This study examines the discontinuous Galerkin finite element method for solving the one-dimensional Rosenau equation. We establish the existence and uniqueness of solutions within the corresponding semi-discrete framework. Furthermore, utilizing energy estimates, we derive optimal-order error bounds for the method.

This study examines the well-posedness of a coupled system of partial differential equations modeling the interaction between compressible and incompressible fluids. The framework employs a compressible Navier-Stokes formulation for the former and a Stokes equation for the latter, linked by a shared interface. By applying an $\textit{inf-sup}$ condition to the coupling terms, we establish the existence of a solution within a specific Sobolev space. Furthermore, we demonstrate the semigroup property of the resulting solution operator, thereby confirming its well-posedness.

We present a theoretical investigation into the magnetic-field-driven Wigner crystallization of charged interlayer excitons within van der Waals heterostructures. Our analysis reveals that the crystallization threshold is highly sensitive to the magnetic field's orientation relative to the heterobilayer plane. Specifically, when the field is applied parallel to the plane, the critical magnetic field required for crystallization is significantly lower than when the field is applied perpendicularly. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the presence of a dielectric mismatch at the interface between the two monolayers substantially elevates this critical magnetic field.

This study presents a relative calibration of radial velocities (RVs) for the LAMOST Medium-Resolution Stellar Spectra (LAMOST-MRS) dataset, which comprises 1,000,000 stellar spectra. The calibration utilizes the Sun as a reference, leveraging the Sun's well-established RVs from the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager (HMI) to correct for systematic errors in the LAMOST-MRS RVs. The resulting corrected LAMOST-MRS RVs exhibit a mean offset of 0.000 ± 0.001 km s$^{-1}$ and a standard deviation of 0.003 km s$^{-1}$ relative to the Sun. Additionally, the study evaluates the impact of the LAMOST-MRS spectral resolution on RV accuracy, revealing that the mean offset increases to 0.001 ± 0.002 km s$^{-1}$ and the standard deviation rises to 0.004 km s$^{-1}$ when the spectral resolution exceeds 10,000. These findings indicate that the LAMOST-MRS RVs are highly precise and reliable for scientific applications.

This study addresses the inverse scattering problem by determining the spatial distribution of the wavenumber-dependent refractive index from measured scattered fields. We introduce a novel neural network architecture designed to solve this inverse problem across a broad frequency spectrum. The approach utilizes a U-Net framework with an encoder-decoder structure, incorporating skip connections and an additional intermediate layer to enhance performance. The model is trained to accept the scattered field as input and generate the corresponding refractive index profile. The network's design ensures equivariance to shifts in the refractive index, thereby guaranteeing physically consistent results. The proposed method is validated through numerical simulations and experimental data.

Accelerated degradation testing (ADT) is a vital method for estimating the lifetime distribution of products and systems. This study introduces a novel ADT framework based on a bivariate gamma process featuring a gamma copula to model the dependency between two degradation paths. The proposed model accounts for both positive and negative correlations, offering greater flexibility than prior approaches. Furthermore, we derive the maximum likelihood estimators for model parameters and their asymptotic distributions, alongside the prediction of future degradation trajectories. The efficacy of this method is validated through a simulation study and an empirical analysis of data from a battery ADT experiment.

We investigate the triangular flow $v_3$ in Au+Au and Cu+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200$ GeV using the AMPT model, which incorporates a multiphase transport approach. Our results indicate that the calculated $v_3$ aligns well with experimental data. Furthermore, we examine the influence of parton scattering on $v_3$ and analyze the correlation between $v_3$ and the event-by-event triangular asymmetry parameter $\Delta\psi_3$.

This study examines the polytropic behavior of plasma within the interaction between Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejections (ICMEs) and High-speed Solar Streams (HSSs). We analyze data from 10 distinct ICME-HSS events, focusing on the plasma's polytropic index ($\gamma$) and the associated thermodynamic processes. Our findings indicate that the plasma is predominantly heated adiabatically ($\gamma \approx 1.0$) during the initial phase of the interaction. Conversely, the interaction phase is characterized by sub-adiabatic behavior ($\gamma < 1.0$), suggesting that the plasma is heated by external sources. In the subsequent expansion phase, the plasma exhibits super-adiabatic behavior ($\gamma > 1.0$), implying that the plasma is compressed by external forces. We also observed that the plasma's polytropic index is influenced by the speed of the ICME and the solar wind dynamic pressure.

The Random Waypoint Mobility Model (RWMM) is a widely adopted method for simulating mobile node behavior in ad hoc networks. This paper examines the statistical properties of the RWMM, specifically focusing on the distribution of node positions and distances between pairs of nodes. We demonstrate that the two-dimensional position distribution is uniform, whereas the one-dimensional distribution of inter-node distances follows a specific pattern. Furthermore, we derive the exact cumulative distribution function (CDF) for the distance separating any two nodes within the model.

This study examines the effective mass distribution of $K^+K^-$ pairs produced in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, utilizing the CMS detector. The analysis focuses on the region surrounding the kinematic threshold, specifically for invariant masses between 0.95 GeV/$c^2$ and 1.25 GeV/$c^2$, with a particular emphasis on the threshold area. The observed data are compared against predictions from a phenomenological model that accounts for the $f_0(980)$ and $f_0(1370)$ scalar mesons, as well as non-resonant contributions. The findings indicate that the $f_0(980)$ meson exhibits a significantly enhanced production rate relative to the $f_0(1370)$ meson. Additionally, the results are benchmarked against measurements from the LHCb detector.

This study investigates the collective inertial mass of a compound nucleus during a reaction, accounting for the nuclear effective mass. We demonstrate that the nuclear effective mass significantly alters the mass's value, particularly when the reaction involves nucleon transfer. Furthermore, we propose a new framework for calculating this inertial mass, which incorporates the nucleon transfer process and the resulting change in effective mass.

The Abstraction Reasoning Corpus (ARC) serves as a benchmark for assessing artificial intelligence systems, featuring a dataset of 10,000 tasks that demand high-level reasoning. This study introduces a new approach to solving ARC problems by abstracting them into constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs). We evaluate this method against two baselines: a random search algorithm and a neural network trained on the task data. Our results demonstrate that our CSP-based approach outperforms both baselines, achieving an accuracy of 50.4% on the ARC-10k test set.

This work examines the regularity properties of entropy solutions to scalar conservation laws featuring discontinuous flux, specifically focusing on how the local smoothness of these solutions depends on the arrangement of flux discontinuities. We demonstrate that for any configuration of discontinuities, the solutions possess fractional Sobolev regularity with an exponent $\alpha$ that is contingent upon this discontinuity structure. Furthermore, we establish that these solutions belong to $BV_{\text{loc}}$ if and only if the discontinuities do not form a periodic pattern.

The branching fractions for $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ and $B^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ were measured using a data sample of $1.0 \times 10^{9}$ $B\bar{B}$ pairs collected by the LHCb detector. The analysis relies on a simultaneous fit to the $D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ mass spectrum across both $B_{s}^{0}$ and $B^{0}$ decays, employing a double ratio method to determine the branching fraction of $B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$ relative to $B^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}$. The resulting values are $\mathcal{B}(B_{s}^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}) = (0.081 \pm 0.006 \pm 0.004) \times 10^{-2}$ and $\mathcal{B}(B^{0} \to D_{s}^{-} K^{+}) = (0.0060 \pm 0.001 \pm 0.001) \times 10^{-2}$, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second is systematic.

This study examines the spectral efficiency of cell-free massive MIMO systems employing multicarrier-division duplex (MCD-D) for backhaul links. We introduce a novel MCD-D framework that utilizes a single subcarrier for uplink (UL) transmission and multiple subcarriers for downlink (DL) transmission. This approach is designed to mitigate the inherent uplink-downlink interference caused by the asymmetric nature of massive MIMO systems, where the number of subcarriers allocated to the DL is significantly greater than that of the UL. We demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves superior spectral efficiency compared to conventional single-carrier UL and DL configurations. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of the number of subcarriers assigned to the DL on the spectral efficiency. Finally, we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the spectral efficiency as the number of subcarriers approaches infinity.

Differential privacy (DP) is a rigorous framework for ensuring privacy in statistical data analysis. While the shuffle model has recently emerged as a promising alternative to the standard centralized and local models, it offers superior privacy guarantees by having a data server shuffle inputs before they are processed. This paper presents the first algorithm for sum queries within the shuffle model that achieves optimal sample complexity. Specifically, it demonstrates that sum queries on a dataset of size $n$ can be answered with $\tilde{O}(1/\varepsilon)$ samples to ensure $(\varepsilon, \delta)$-DP, where $\delta$ is a negligible value. This result matches the lower bound established by Kasiviswanathan et al. (2021) for the private sum problem in the centralized model. Furthermore, the study introduces a novel technique for precisely accounting privacy loss in the shuffle model, which is of independent value.

Orthogonal Time Frequency Multiplexing (OTFS) has emerged as a leading modulation scheme for future wireless systems, offering robust performance in high-mobility environments. This paper introduces Orthogonal Time Sequency Multiplexing (OTSM), a novel variation of OTF that operates in the time-sectency domain. Leveraging the Fourier transform's ability to convert time-domain signals into the frequency-sectency domain, OTSM achieves a lower computational complexity than OTFS. The study provides a comprehensive analysis of OTSM, including its mathematical formulation, the derivation of its correlation matrix, and the calculation of its peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Furthermore, the paper proposes a low-complexity receiver design for OTSM that utilizes a simplified channel estimation approach and a detection algorithm based on the minimum mean square error (MMSE) criterion. Simulation results demonstrate that OTSM delivers bit error rate (BER) performance comparable to OTFS while significantly reducing computational demands.

This study examines the operator norm within the Banach algebra of $\ell^1$ on a discrete semigroup $S$ equipped with a weight $\omega$, specifically under the faithful representation on $L^1(G)$ where $G$ is an abelian group. We demonstrate that the norm for elements with finite support is determined by the norm of the corresponding convolution operator on $L^1(G)$. Furthermore, we establish that the norm for arbitrary elements in $\ell^1(S, \omega)$ is governed by the norm of the associated Fourier transform operator acting on $L^p(G)$.

This study numerically investigates the dynamics of a molten metal melt pool during laser spot melting using a conduction model. The research examines how varying laser power and beam diameter influence the melt pool's shape and dimensions. The findings indicate that the melt pool's geometry is primarily governed by the ratio of laser power to beam diameter. Additionally, the study analyzes the impact of surface tension and Marangoni convection on melt pool behavior. The results demonstrate that surface tension and the Marangoni effect significantly alter the melt pool's shape and size.

This study examines a wireless system designed for public transport vehicles (PTVs), where mobile edge computing (MEC) servers are mounted on these vehicles to support connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs). The system architecture involves CAVs transmitting data to the MEC servers via the vehicle-mounted MEC server, which is then connected to a wireless energy transfer (WET) base station (WET-BS) for power. To enhance signal quality, an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is deployed to optimize the wireless channel. The primary objective is to maximize the total energy efficiency (EE) of the MEC servers by jointly optimizing the transmit power of the WET-BS, the phase shifts of the IRS, and the power allocation of the MEC servers. The resulting optimization problem is non-convex; however, it is transformed into a convex form through a change of variables. The solution employs a block coordinate descent (BCD) approach, where each subproblem is solved using the weighted sum rate method, the weighted geometric mean method, and the weighted geometric mean method. The proposed algorithm is validated through numerical simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness.

The query regarding the approximate degree of a Boolean function is a fundamental issue in computational complexity theory. This paper establishes a novel lower bound for the approximate degree of Boolean functions defined by DNF formulas. Specifically, for a DNF formula $\phi$ with $m$ terms, each containing $n$ variables, and a minimum Hamming distance $\delta$ from the complement of the function represented by $\phi$, the approximate degree is bounded below by $\Omega(\sqrt{n\delta(1-\delta)/m})$. This finding extends and refines earlier work by Sherstov, who derived a bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{n\delta(1-\delta)})$ applicable to read-once DNF formulas. Furthermore, the study demonstrates that this lower bound is tight for a specific class of DNF formulas, including those with a constant number of terms, those with a constant maximum variable count per term, and those with a constant maximum number of variables across the entire formula.

This study introduces a new method for detecting bistable structures in dynamical systems by utilizing the Conley index theory. We establish a theoretical framework for the Conley index of bistable structures and develop an algorithm to compute it numerically. This approach is applied to analyze the bistable behavior of a mathematical model describing the dynamics of the *lac* operon.

This study examines the equation of state for strange quark matter under the influence of a magnetic field and at finite temperature, specifically considering a scenario where the quarks are spin-polarized. The analysis incorporates the MIT bag model, the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model, and the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model augmented with the NJL model. The resulting equations of state are applied to determine the maximum mass and corresponding radius of strange stars. The findings indicate that the predicted stellar mass and radius are highly sensitive to the specific model employed.

Audio-visual correlation (AVC) involves learning the relationship between audio and video data, a field that has seen significant advancements in recent years. This paper reviews recent breakthroughs in AVC, specifically focusing on the latest deep learning methodologies. We examine the primary challenges associated with AVC and propose potential future research directions.

This study introduces a probabilistic framework for evaluating solution reliability within the Linear Ordering Problem (LOP). We propose a novel probabilistic metric, the probability of dominance (PD), which assesses a solution's reliability by calculating the likelihood that a randomly selected alternative is dominated by it. We demonstrate that the PD of a solution is equivalent to the expected value of its dominance count. Furthermore, we develop two algorithms to estimate the PD of a given solution: the first utilizes a Monte Carlo simulation approach, while the second employs a new method based on the linear ordering polytope. We also present a new LOPlp-based polyhedral formulation designed to compute the exact PD for a specific solution. Finally, computational experiments are conducted to compare the performance of our proposed algorithms.

This study examines the impact of disorder on the superconducting phase diagram of NbN thin films, specifically investigating the transition from a superconductor to an insulator. We observe that the critical temperature ($T_c$) exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on disorder, characterized by a distinct peak. Furthermore, the superfluid density displays a complex phase diagram, where the $T_c$ value is notably higher in the superconductor-insulator transition (SIT) regime compared to the superconductor-metal transition (SMT) regime. These findings suggest that disorder-induced phase fluctuations are most pronounced near the SIT.

Temporal graph databases are increasingly prevalent across various domains, including social networks, transportation systems, and biological research. Temporal Regular Path Queries (TRPQs) serve as a novel extension of Regular Path Queries (RPQs), designed to retrieve paths that hold true at specific moments or time intervals within these temporal graph databases. This paper introduces a formal framework for TRPQs, establishing the decidability of their evaluation. Furthermore, we delineate specific tractable scenarios and demonstrate that the problem becomes coNP-complete in several significant special cases.

We introduce a novel approach to the simultaneous deceleration of polyatomic free radicals and lithium atoms, a technique that leverages the magnetic interaction between the lithium's unpaired electron and the radical's unpaired electron. This method utilizes a sequence of alternating magnetic field coils to generate a decelerating force. The study demonstrates that this approach is viable for slowing down the methyl radical ($\text{CH}_3$) paired with lithium atoms. Furthermore, this technique offers significant potential for slowing other free radicals, thereby enabling investigations into their chemical and physical characteristics.

The Swift satellite's X-ray Telescope (XRT) is capable of detecting X-ray transients, yet the instrument's limited field of view and the absence of a continuous all-sky monitoring mode have historically restricted the volume of data available for such studies. This paper introduces a new, real-time transient detection algorithm designed to identify X-ray transients within the Swift-XRT light curves of all known sources. By applying this method to the entire Swift-XRT catalogue, we have compiled a new Living Catalogue of Swift-XRT Point Transients, which is publicly accessible at http://www.mpe.mpg.de/~swiftxrt/LSXRTPS.html. This resource contains light curves for 1,000 Swift-XRT point sources, with 100 of them identified as X-ray transients. We demonstrate the utility of this catalogue by analyzing the light curves of these 100 transients, revealing that 70% are consistent with power-law decays, while the remaining 30% exhibit complex, multi-component light curves. Furthermore, we present a new method for estimating the peak flux of X-ray transients, which is particularly valuable for determining the luminosity of distant events.

We investigate the spin-1/2 J1-J2 XY model defined on a square lattice, focusing on the plaquette valence bond state (PVB S). This state emerges within the region of the phase diagram where the long-range order coexists with plaquette order. We demonstrate that the PVB S serves as the ground state for a specific segment of this region, characterized by a plaquette order parameter of $\eta = 0.905$. Furthermore, we analyze the properties of the PVB S, including its excitation spectrum and correlation functions.

This study introduces a three-dimensional panel data model designed to analyze bilateral trade flows. The framework incorporates country-specific fixed effects for both trading partners, alongside a time-varying fixed effect common to all pairs. By applying this model, we decompose observed bilateral trade into three distinct components: (1) the individual fixed effects of each trading nation, (2) the global common shock affecting all pairs in a specific period, and (3) the idiosyncratic interaction term unique to each specific country pair. We establish the consistency of these estimators and demonstrate their asymptotic normal distribution. Furthermore, we apply this methodology to real-world data to evaluate the relative significance of these three components in explaining total trade volumes.

This study examines the construction of a four-dimensional noncommutative $U(1)$ gauge theory featuring a deformed star product, utilizing the $L_{\infty}$ bootstrap framework. We demonstrate that this noncommutative $U(1)$ theory can be formulated as a free theory perturbed by nonlocal interactions, which are expressed through the Hochschild cohomology of the commutative algebra associated with the undeformed model. Furthermore, we analyze the theory's behavior in the high-energy limit, revealing that the resulting effective action corresponds to a noncommutative deformation of the Born-Infeld action.

This study introduces a coherent equalization framework for linear quantum systems, designed to counteract channel distortions and mitigate intersymbol interference (ISI) in optical fiber communications. By leveraging the inherent quantum properties of light, the proposed method achieves superior equalization performance compared to conventional approaches. Specifically, the equalizer is formulated as a quantum linear system that reconstructs the transmitted signal from the received one. This formulation is achieved by synthesizing the equalizer's transfer function to satisfy a set of constraints, thereby ensuring the fulfillment of the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of a valid quantum linear system. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates that the equalizer can be implemented using a finite collection of passive optical components, including beam splitters, phase shifters, and mirrors.

Perceiving the passage of time is a fundamental human capability that is essential for daily functioning. However, this perception is susceptible to alteration by various factors, including age, sleep deprivation, and mental health conditions. This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to forecast changes in time perception using data from wearable devices. The model is trained on data from 100 participants who completed a time perception task while wearing a smartwatch. The system utilizes features derived from heart rate variability and heart rate patterns to predict the time perception scores. The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.43, with a 95% confidence interval of ±0.05. Furthermore, the model was applied to a separate dataset of 20 participants to identify correlations between time perception and mental health status. The findings indicate that time perception is significantly associated with mental health, with a p-value of 0.001 and a 95% confidence interval of ±0.05. These results demonstrate that time perception can be effectively predicted using smartwatch data and that it holds substantial relevance for mental health monitoring.

This study investigates the relationship between decision speed and quality in high-stakes, complex scenarios. Drawing on field data from a military simulation, we examine how decision speed and quality interact with varying levels of information and uncertainty. Our findings indicate that decision speed and quality are negatively correlated, particularly when information and uncertainty are low. Furthermore, we observe that decision quality improves as the availability of information and uncertainty decrease. These results suggest that the trade-off between speed and quality is most pronounced in conditions of low information and uncertainty, offering valuable insights for designing decision support systems and training programs for high-stakes environments.

This paper examines the relationship between legal frameworks and fairness definitions in machine learning. We analyze how legal principles shape these definitions, specifically exploring the alignment between the Equalized Odds metric and the legal doctrine of Disparate Impact. Our findings demonstrate that while Equalized Odds is a necessary condition for satisfying Disparate Impact, it is not sufficient. Furthermore, we argue that the legal doctrine of Discrete Impact is more comprehensive than the Equalized Odds metric because it accounts for statistical significance.

We introduce a novel approach to detect the magnetic dipole moment of neutrinos by investigating the magnetic anisotropy in trivalent lanthanoid ions. This magnetic anisotropy arises from the interaction between the magnetic field and the magnetic moment of the lanthanoid ions, which is modulated by the occupation of the $4f$ shell. This occupation level is governed by the temperature and the thermal emission of neutrino pairs. Consequently, measuring the magnetic anisotropy allows for the determination of the $4f$ shell's population, thereby enabling the extraction of the neutrino magnetic moment.

We investigate strangeness in light hypernuclei using a chiral effective field theory framework. This approach utilizes a nucleon-meson interaction Lagrangian that incorporates single- and double-strangeness mesons alongside nucleons and hyperons, with couplings fixed by experimental data on $\Lambda$ hyperons. Our calculations successfully reproduce binding energies and separation energies for hypernuclei up to $A=8$, including double-strangeness cases. Furthermore, we analyze the properties of the $\Lambda\Lambda$-hypernucleus $^4_{\Lambda\Lambda}$He, offering a theoretical prediction for its mass.

Social media platforms often fail to fully protect user privacy, prompting individuals to adopt various strategies to mitigate these risks. This paper introduces MetaPriv, a new framework designed to model the privacy behaviors of social media users. MetaPriv represents a user's privacy stance as a meta-preference, which is a higher-order preference that dictates the preference for specific privacy policies. By utilizing this meta-preference, MetaPriv can forecast a user's privacy actions in response to new policies. The framework was trained and evaluated using a dataset of 1,000 Twitter users, demonstrating its effectiveness in predicting privacy actions with an F1 score of 0.71.

We investigate the point process of points generated by the coalescent process associated with a branching mechanism in fluctuating conditions. This setup corresponds to branching dynamics evolving within a time-homogeneous Poisson process. We establish that the resulting point process is non-homogeneous Poisson, and we derive its intensity function and marginal distribution functions for the inter-arrival times.
This paper examines the hard-core model on the Cayley tree, where the spin variable set is countable. We demonstrate that the system possesses a continuum of Gibbsian equilibrium states.

The LAMOST-DR7 central velocity dispersion catalog, comprising 1,000 galaxies, is presented here. These objects were selected from the LAMOST-DR7 red sequence, defined by their specific color and magnitude ranges, and their central velocity dispersions were derived from LAMOST spectra. The catalog includes data on redshift, apparent magnitude, color, angular size, and central velocity dispersion. Additionally, we provide estimates for stellar mass, effective radius, and stellar mass-to-light ratio, all calculated using the $K$-band luminosity and the $Sersic$ profile fitting method. This catalog serves as a valuable resource for investigating the mass-to-light ratio, mass-metallicity relation, and the $M_{\rm e}-\sigma$ relation.

This study introduces a new approach to calculating isotope shifts in atomic spectra using relativistic coupled-cluster (RCC) theory. By applying the frequency-dependent density response method, we derive the scalar and vector components of the polarizability for indium isotopes. These components are then utilized to calculate isotope shifts, with our results aligning closely with experimental data. The methodology is validated by comparing our findings with existing experimental results and prior theoretical studies. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the RCC approach is capable of accurately modeling the complex many-body effects essential for precise isotope shift calculations.

This work examines graph states, which are specific quantum states linked to graphs. We demonstrate that the variety of principal minors for graph states is determined by the graph's structure. Specifically, we establish that the dimension of this variety is determined by the number of vertices minus the graph's matching number, a result that is achieved with a minimal codimension of one. Furthermore, we prove that the matrix rank is preserved under generic conditions, a property that holds true for all connected graphs lacking induced 4-cycles.

A *transversal* is defined as a subset of a set system that intersects every member of the system exactly once. This paper presents a straightforward sufficient condition ensuring the existence of a transversal within a set system composed of finite subsets of a given set. Specifically, if a set system $\mathcal{F}$ satisfies the property that for any $k \geq 1$, every collection of $k$ distinct sets from $\mathcal{F}$ contains at least $k$ common elements, then $\mathcal{F}$ is guaranteed to possess a transversal. This result serves as a natural extension of Hall's Marriage Theorem.

The escalating demand for mobile video streaming has driven the development of transcoding services that convert video into various formats and bitrates to optimize playback on diverse devices. This study examines transcoding performance within heterogeneous cloud environments, specifically focusing on the Amazon EC2 cloud platform. We introduce a framework for modeling transcoding latency and construct a queuing network to represent transcoding workflows across multiple cloud providers. By applying the Mean Value Analysis (MVA) technique, we evaluate the system's performance under varying loads. Our findings indicate that while the Amazon EC2 platform is capable of handling transcoding tasks, its high cost renders it less competitive compared to alternative providers.

This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior of the probability that a random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ ($d \geq 3$) remains within a ball of radius $R$ for a duration of $n$ steps, specifically analyzing the count of excursions across the sphere's boundary. We demonstrate that for any $t > 0$, the probability that the normalized discrepancy between the actual and expected number of such excursions falls within the interval $[-tR^{d-1}, \infty)$ decays at a rate of $e^{-ct^2R^{d-1}}$. This finding represents a moderate deviation principle for the count of boundary crossings.

This paper investigates the ground state of the energy functional associated with the energy supercritical Gross--Pitaevskii equation. By applying the mountain pass theorem, we establish the existence of a ground state. Furthermore, we determine its unique ground state, denoted as $\psi$, and demonstrate that the Hessian of the energy functional evaluated at $\psi$ possesses an odd Morse index.

This paper introduces a formal framework for the automated evaluation of clinical trial designs, specifically tailored for binary outcomes. The approach employs a rigorous, simulation-based method to determine the statistical power of a trial design, ensuring the Type I error rate remains at or below a specified threshold. The methodology is demonstrated through two case studies: a two-arm, two-stage trial and a multi-arm, two-stage trial.

The Metaverse represents a novel digital realm where users engage in immersive, interactive experiences. While current research predominantly focuses on the social and economic dimensions of this ecosystem, the technical underpinnings remain largely unexplored. This paper introduces a distributed rendering framework designed to facilitate such interactive environments. By leveraging the inherent parallelism of graphics processing, the proposed system distributes rendering tasks across multiple nodes to enhance performance. We evaluate the approach using a demanding scene featuring a high-fidelity human model, demonstrating significant performance gains.

This study examines the annotation and alignment accuracy of complex orchestral music by comparing two sets of scores annotated by different experts. The analysis reveals that even for experienced annotators, achieving high-precision alignment between scores is challenging. The paper also introduces a new method for detecting discrepancies in orchestral music annotations, which is validated using a dataset of 100 measures from two versions of Bach's *The Art of Fugue*, annotated by two specialists. The results indicate that the method successfully identifies 95% of the differences between the scores.

The Full-Duplex Radio (FDR) represents a significant advancement in wireless communication, enabling simultaneous transmission and reception on the same frequency channel. This capability substantially enhances spectral efficiency and reduces latency, making FDR a promising technology for future wireless networks. However, FDR faces a primary challenge: self-interference (SI), which occurs when the transmitter's signal interferes with its own receiver. This paper introduces a novel, advanced self-interference cancellation (SIxC) framework designed for FDR systems. The proposed method employs a hybrid architecture combining a traditional analog cancellation stage with a deep neural network (DNN) for digital cancellation. The DNN is trained to model and eliminate residual interference that persists after the analog stage. Additionally, we present a new multiantenna technique that leverages the spatial diversity of multiple antennas to further mitigate SI. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid SIxC approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, while the introduced multiantenna strategy offers substantial SI reduction.

Colloidal droplets, which are ubiquitous in nature and industry, are typically stabilized by surfactants that form a viscoelastic shell. This shell is prone to buckling and invagination when the droplet undergoes volume reduction, a process driven by the shell's elastic resistance to bending. This study investigates the invagination of buckled droplets through a combination of experimental observations and theoretical modeling. We demonstrate that the critical radius at which invagination initiates is determined by the shell's bending rigidity and the droplet's size. Furthermore, we find that the invagination speed is governed by the shell's viscosity and the rate of volume compression.

Lyman-alpha (Ly$\alpha$) emission from protoplanetary disks (PPDs) is a promising probe for studying disk evolution and planet formation. This study investigates the physical mechanisms driving Ly$\alpha$ emission in PPDs, specifically examining how the gas density profile, dust distribution, and UV radiation from the central star influence the resulting spectra. We utilize a Monte Carlo radiative transfer code to simulate the Ly$\alpha$ emission from a disk with a fixed gas density profile, varying the dust distribution and UV radiation field. Our results indicate that Ly$\alpha$ emission is primarily generated in the disk's upper layers, where the gas density is low. Consequently, the Ly$\alpha$ line profile is heavily shaped by scattering in the upper layers, with the line wings being particularly sensitive to the gas density profile. We demonstrate that Ly$\alpha$ emission is strongly suppressed in disks with high dust content, as the line center becomes optically thick. Furthermore, we find that Ly$\alpha$ emission is significantly reduced in disks with high UV fluxes, as the line center becomes optically thick. We also show that Ly$\alpha$ emission is significantly reduced in disks with high UV fluxes, as the line center becomes optically thick. This paper introduces a fingerprint-based millimeter wave (mWave) positioning system enhanced by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). The proposed architecture leverages the RIS to generate multiple line-of-sight (LoS) paths, thereby improving positioning accuracy. The study first establishes a comprehensive database of radio signal fingerprints, which are then utilized to estimate the user's location. The authors further analyze the relationship between the user's position and the received signal power, deriving a closed-form expression for the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) of the estimated location. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed RIS-assisted mWave positioning system achieves superior accuracy compared to conventional systems lacking RIS support.

This study examines the generation of twisted particles within magnetic fields, focusing on scenarios where the field strength is significantly lower than the particle's cyclotron frequency. We demonstrate that the magnetic field induces a phase shift in the particle's wave function, resulting in orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit coupling. Furthermore, we analyze the spin dynamics of a relativistic electron in a linearly polarized electromagnetic field, revealing that the electron acquires orbital angular momentum and spin-orbit coupling. We also explore the implications of these findings for electron storage rings and propose a method for measuring the electron's spin-orbit coupling using circular dichroism.

This study examines the optimal siting of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations, the pricing strategies for charging services, and the design of the associated market mechanisms. The research focuses on a scenario where a single charging station operator supplies multiple EV drivers, each possessing distinct preferences regarding location and price. The analysis begins by determining the ideal placement of charging stations to maximize the operator's profit, followed by an investigation into pricing policies that account for drivers' heterogeneity. The study concludes by proposing a market framework that facilitates EV drivers in selecting both the most suitable charging station and pricing plan.

This study examines a broad class of sequential treatment allocation methods that prioritize balancing cumulative totals of a covariate alongside ensuring balanced overall treatment counts. These tie-breaking mechanisms are defined by two parameters: one governing the primary balance focus and the other determining how strictly this primary goal is enforced. We establish that for such a design to achieve complete balance across a fixed finite sample, the tie-breaking priority must be set to zero, effectively making it secondary. Furthermore, we demonstrate that an allocation method utilizing a tie-breaking rule with a strictly positive priority yields asymptotic normality for cumulative treatment effects within a sequential randomization framework.

We derive the three-point correlation functions for arbitrary spinor current multiplets within a unitary ${\mathcal N}=1$ superconformal framework. Our analysis demonstrates that these results are fully determined by the superconformal algebra and the unitarity bounds, relying solely on two fundamental parameters: the normalization factor and a quantum number known as the R-charge.

Machine teaching represents a novel paradigm in artificial intelligence that focuses on the efficient generation of data and labels to train machine learning models. Although current research has primarily concentrated on optimizing these processes for adult users, this study investigates whether machine teaching is accessible to children. We introduce a new framework designed to evaluate the effectiveness of machine teaching strategies when employed by children. Our findings indicate that, contrary to expectations, the strategies currently favored by adults do not consistently yield superior results for young learners. Instead, we demonstrate that adapting these approaches to suit children's specific needs can significantly enhance their learning outcomes.

Lifelong reinforcement learning (RL) represents a significant advancement in the field, enabling agents to acquire a continuous stream of skills. This paper examines the current landscape of lifelong RL, focusing on two critical dimensions: the specific challenges posed by lifelong RL and the potential for cross-fertilization between lifelong RL and continual learning. We argue that integrating insights from both domains is essential for addressing the unique hurdles faced by lifelong RL agents. Furthermore, we outline a research agenda aimed at advancing the understanding of lifelong RL systems.

We demonstrate the coherent transformation of a photonic qubit encoded in polarization into one encoded in spatial mode, occurring within a single integrated nanophotonic chip. This conversion is achieved through a hybrid architecture combining a silicon nitride waveguide with a piezoelectric aluminum nitride resonator. The process relies on the optomechanical interaction between the waveguide's optical field and the mechanical resonance of the resonator, which mediates the transfer between the qubit's polarization and spatial-mode degrees of freedom.

This study examines the electronic transport characteristics of DNA molecules featuring mismatched base pairs. We introduce a model that incorporates the influence of solvent and counterions, which are essential for DNA stability. By employing a combination of the tight-binding approximation and the Green's function technique, we analyze the system's electronic structure and electronic transport properties. Our findings reveal that introducing mispairs causes a significant reduction in electronic conductance, a result that aligns with recent experimental data. Furthermore, we demonstrate that conductance is highly sensitive to variations in the solvent and counterion parameters. These results offer valuable insights into the mechanisms of electronic transport within DNA.

Accurate registration of multi-view point clouds is essential for 3D reconstruction and object recognition. While the Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm is widely used, it is highly sensitive to outliers, which are prevalent in real-world scenarios. This paper introduces a novel, robust, and efficient ICP variant that integrates K-means clustering. The proposed method first clusters points into groups, then aligns each cluster individually with the target. This approach significantly reduces computational cost and enhances robustness against outliers. Experimental results demonstrate that the new method outperforms existing robust ICP variants in both accuracy and efficiency.

We report on the magnetic structure of Tb$_3$RuO$_7$, a compound featuring alternating-bond spin-3/2 Ru chains situated within nonuniform internal magnetic fields generated by Tb$^{3+}$ ions. This system exhibits a complex magnetic phase diagram, including a partially disordered state. This disordered phase emerges from a first-order transition at $T_{\rm c1} = 10.5$ K, which is followed by a second-order transition at $T_{\rm c2} = 9.5$ K. The magnetic structure is characterized by a combination of ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic components, with the ferromagnetic part arising from the interaction between nearest-neighbor Ru ions. The internal magnetic field from Tb$^{3+}$ ions is responsible for the first-order transition at $T_{\rm c1}$, while the interaction between next-nearest-neighbor Ru ions drives the second-order transition at $T_{\rm c2}$.

This study examines the necessary and sufficient optimality criteria for constrained mathematical programming problems where both the objective and constraint functions are difference convex (DC). The analysis relies on concepts from variational analysis, specifically the normal cone derived from the epigraph of a convex hull of a function. Additionally, we explore the connections between these conditions and the regularity properties inherent to DC functions.

We investigate the dynamics of fundamental strings and D-instantons within the near-horizon limit of a D$7$-brane intersecting a D$(-1)$-brane, which is dual to a $0$-dimensional conformal field theory. This framework is examined in the context of the proposed $AdS_1$/CFT$_0$ correspondence.

We examine the interaction of two expanding domains within $\mathbb{R}^d$ that are governed by their respective smooth, time-dependent curvature conditions. The study establishes that when these domains collide, the resulting interface maintains smoothness and evolves according to curvature flow. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the collision event occurs at a distinct time point rather than asymptotically over an infinite duration.

This study introduces a novel Bayesian controller fusion approach designed to integrate the robustness of deep neural networks with the interpretability and stability of linear controllers. By framing the fusion as a Bayesian inference problem, we derive a closed-form solution for the optimal controller weights. This method is particularly effective in robotic control scenarios where linear controllers are prone to local minima, while neural networks risk overfitting. We demonstrate the approach's efficacy through two case studies: a 2D cart-pole balancing task and a 3D robotic arm reaching task.

Perfusion imaging is a critical component of stroke diagnosis, enabling clinicians to distinguish between salvageable brain tissue and areas of infarction. This process involves calculating hemodynamic parameters from raw perfusion maps, which are typically generated using deconvolution algorithms. However, these conventional methods are computationally intensive and prone to instability, often resulting in noisy or inaccurate parameter estimates. To address these limitations, we introduce a differentiable deconvolution framework that leverages deep learning to derive stroke perfusion metrics. Our approach utilizes a neural network to approximate the inverse Laplace transform required for deconvolution, thereby enabling the direct optimization of perfusion maps through end-to-end training. We validate this method using clinical datasets and demonstrate that it achieves superior accuracy and robustness compared to traditional techniques.

We present the complete three-loop splitting functions for the zero-jettiness beam function, which are required for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) calculations of differential cross sections involving a hard process and a single collinear parton. Our results are expressed in terms of harmonic polylogarithms, with all color factors factored out. These findings are essential for achieving full N$^3$LO precision in various phenomenological applications, such as Higgs boson production and jet substructure analyses.

The concept of the power graph for a finite group $G$, denoted $\Gamma(P(G))$, is defined as a graph where vertices represent the elements of $G$, and an edge connects two distinct elements $x$ and $y$ if one is a power of the other. This paper investigates the chordal properties of such power graphs. Specifically, we demonstrate that the power graph of a finite group $G$ is chordal if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to one of the following structures: $1$, $C_{p^n}$, $C_{p^n} \rtimes C_q$ (where $p$ is a prime and $q$ is a prime power), or $C_{p^n} \rtimes C_q \rtimes C_r$ (where $p$, $q$, and $r$ are primes).

This study introduces a new method for separating target sources from background noise and other interfering signals. The approach involves training a neural network to identify the specific conditions under which target sources are most distinguishable. Once these optimal conditions are established, a separate separation network is utilized to isolate the target from the mixed audio. The network is trained using a dataset of mixed recordings, where the target source is known. The proposed method demonstrates superior performance compared to existing techniques, particularly in scenarios involving multiple background sources.

The concept of quantum coherence has been extensively explored, with recent research extending it to relative coherence between two states. This study introduces a generalized framework for measuring coherence relative to an arbitrary quantum measurement, defined by a set of Kraus operators. We establish multiple coherence monotones within this framework and develop a corresponding relative version of the Coherence Distillation number. Additionally, we demonstrate that relative quantum mutual information serves as a bound for relative coherence, thereby extending the findings of Luo (2015) regarding standard quantum mutual information.

We report the detection of Type C quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the X-ray binary H 1743–322 during two distinct outbursts, utilizing data from the Rossi X-ray Timing Explorer (RXTE) and the Swift X-ray Telescope (XRT). The 2000 outburst yielded a Type C QPO with a period of 1.85 s, whereas the 2011 outburst exhibited a period of 1.75 s. These findings align with earlier observations from the 1998 outburst, which identified a period of 1.80 s. The consistency of these QPO periods across multiple outbursts suggests that the accretion flow geometry remains stable. Furthermore, the 2000 outburst data reveal a correlation between the QPO period and the X-ray flux, a relationship that is absent in the 2011 outburst. We propose that the 2000 outburst QPOs originate from the accretion disk, whereas the 2011 QPOs arise from the accretion column.

This paper introduces an open-domain question answering (QA) system designed to support e-governance initiatives. The system comprises a question classifier, a document retrieval module, and a passage ranking component. It is built upon a QA dataset derived from the Indian government's official website, which has been annotated with answer spans. We present a novel QA dataset and outline the architecture of our proposed system. Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the results, including performance metrics and insights into the system's capabilities.

The EAGLE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, which incorporate a semi-analytic model for galaxy formation, successfully reproduce the observed stellar mass function of galaxies. However, this success comes at the cost of overproducing the number of galaxies with stellar masses below $10^{10} \, M_\odot$. This study investigates the baryonic content of these low-mass galaxies to determine if the discrepancy stems from baryon retention or conversion into stars. We find that the stellar-to-baryon ratio in these systems is approximately 0.1, consistent with the cosmic average. Consequently, the primary issue lies in the retention of baryons rather than their conversion into stars. We demonstrate that the simulated galaxies retain a higher fraction of their baryons compared to Milky Way-mass galaxies, which we attribute to the galaxies' lower escape velocities.

A separator of a graph $G$ is defined as a vertex set $S$ such that removing $S$ disconnects $G$ into multiple components, each having a vertex count no greater than $|V(G)| - |S| - 1$. We introduce a new algorithm designed to identify all separators of size at most $k$ that are leftmost, meaning no other separator of equal size precedes them in lexicographical order. This approach achieves a runtime of $2^{O(k)} \cdot n^{O(1)}$ and represents a significant improvement over the prior best complexity of $2^{O(k \log k)} \cdot n^{O(1)}$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our method can be adapted to enumerate all separators of size $\leq k$ in $2^{O(k)} \cdot n^{O(1)}$ time, improving upon the previous bound of $2^{O(k \log k)} \cdot n^{O(1)}$.

We present a study of transient events within the centers of 100 galaxies, comprising 50 post-starburst (PSB) and 50 quiescent Balmer-strong (QBS) systems. These samples were selected from the SDSS DR12 catalog based on their Balmer absorption line indices. Our analysis reveals that 60% of the PSBs and 40% of the QBSs host a transient, with the majority classified as Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia).
